transcript:
This message comes from Odu.
Running a business shouldn't feel like surviving a software group project.
Start managing your business with one unified system.
Odu is the all-in-one business management software.
Try for free today at Odu.com/NPRPodcasts.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The passengers aboard a Dubai-Tatelavi flight that was caught in a mid-air crisis have made it to Israel.
After an emergency detour to Saudi Arabia,
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says one of the pilots apparently stabbed the other pilot
and then tried to crash the plane.
Here's NPR's Ea Batrawi.
Netanyahu says the plane went into a spin and began to plunge
as one of the pilots was trying to sabotage the aircraft's systems after stabbing his co-pilot.
He says nearly all passengers on board were Israeli
and that the plane landed safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia.
Netanyahu says the suspected attacker is being questioned now by Saudi authorities,
though Saudi Arabia has yet to confirm that.
Flight Dubai says the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia
after a "altercation occurred in the flight deck."
The airline deployed two replacement aircraft to bring the passengers from Tabuk to Tel Aviv
and cautioned that the motives behind the incident are unknown
and remain subject to a formal investigation.
Israel's defense minister, however, called it an attempted jihadist terrorist attack
but provided no further details.
Ea Batrawi, NPR News, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
The U.S. military's withdrawal from Iraq is complete
more than two decades after the U.S. invasion
and 12 years after it launched a mission against the ISIS terrorist group.
Annual inflation in the U.S. in August was a little cooler than forecasters had expected
and Pierre Scott Horsley reports on the latest cost of living data from the Commerce Department.
Consumer prices in August were up 3.4 percent from a year ago,
according to the Commerce Department's inflation yardstick,
which is closely washed by the Federal Reserve.
Gasoline and diesel prices inched lower overnight,
but remained much higher than they were before the U.S. launched its war with Iran.
The U.S. economy grew a bit faster this spring than first reported.
Updated figures show GDP grew at an annual rate of 2.2 percent in April, May and June.
Thanks to upward revisions to consumer and government spending and investment.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
A new poll looks at what voters in rural America think about
President Trump's "Make America Healthy Again" movement.
Sarah Jane Trimble with KFF Health News says more.
About eight in ten rural voters said President Trump's health care policies
have had a negative effect, or no impact, on the health of people where they live.
According to a new poll by the Associated Press and KFF,
Kim Solis is a small business owner in Texas.
She says her health care costs have climbed since Trump returned to office,
and she worries about medical emergencies.
Certainly we'd be in a world of hurt trying to take money out of savings
or get it out of our 401(k) just to be able to do something about it.
My brother-in-law, for an example, he has to have a shoulder replacement
and he can't even afford it right now.
The poll surveyed more than 2,000 rural voters in mid-August.
That's KFF's Sarah Jane Trimble reporting.
It's NPR News.
A Tennessee court blocked the execution of a woman
about an hour before she was scheduled to be put to death
for the 1995 murder of a classmate.
Krista Gail Pike was 18 at the time.
Today, the Sixth Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals voted 2-1 to halt the execution
while it reviews whether Pike's age, history of childhood sexual abuse,
and mental illness were fully considered when she was sentenced to death.
The state attorney general has appealed today's decision to the U.S. Supreme Court.
The Death Penalty Information Center says Tennessee has not executed a woman
in at least 200 years.
A year ago today, a tax credit that helped lower the cost of electric vehicles went away,
and Piers Willaruban looks at the impact on car sales.
People heard the EV credit was ending last July.
EV sales spiked, and after it went away, EV sales dropped,
but this year they have stabilized.
About 6% of new cars sold every month now are electric.
Meanwhile, sales of hybrid cars this year have gone up by almost 27%,
according to automotive platform Edmunds.
Sal Iqbal is the general sales manager at the Toyota franchise in Massapequa, New York.
He has seen this with a popular minivan that Toyota now only makes as a hybrid.
We used to have to literally beg people to take a Sienna,
and now we can't keep them on the shelf.
Hybrids with gas engines and battery-powered electric motors are fuel efficient,
and they often have a lower sticker price than many EVs.
Willaruban, NPR News.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.
Visit NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Dubai to Tel Aviv flight diverted to Saudi Arabia after pilot stabbing incident
U.S. military completes withdrawal from Iraq after more than two decades
U.S. annual inflation in August at 3.4 percent, slightly below forecasts
U.S. GDP grew 2.2 percent in second quarter, faster than initially reported
Rural voters say Trump health care policies had negative effect on communities
Tennessee court blocks execution of Krista Gail Pike one hour before scheduled death
Electric vehicle sales stabilize after federal tax credit expired one year ago
Hybrid car sales surge 27 percent as consumers seek lower-cost fuel-efficient vehicles
